launch-va-virginia-beach-first-landing-s.summary: Virginia's most-visited state park protects 2,888 acres of Chesapeake Bay beach, maritime forest, cypress swamp and salt marsh, with 20 miles of trails plus camping, cabins and boating.
launch-va-virginia-beach-first-landing-s.hours: Day-use areas are open daily 7:00 a.m.-dusk. The office and Chesapeake Bay Center are open 8:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m.; the Trail Center is open 8:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m.
launch-va-virginia-beach-first-landing-s.parking: Paid lots serve two different sides of Shore Drive. Use the north side for the Chesapeake Bay Center, beach, campground and cabins; use the south side for the Trail Center, picnic area and most trails. Weekends can reach capacity and arriving vehicles are then turned away.
launch-va-virginia-beach-first-landing-s.arrival: Choose the beach/camping entrance or Trail Center entrance before driving. The Narrows boat ramp is a separate southern access from the 64th Street extension and is not reached through the main contact station.
launch-va-virginia-beach-first-landing-s.restrooms: Restrooms are available at the visitor and trail centers, developed beach and camping areas, picnic area and Narrows boat ramp. Trail interiors do not have continuous facilities or drinking water.
launch-va-virginia-beach-first-landing-s.cost: Parking is $7 on standard days and $10 on weekends from April through October under the current 2026 Virginia State Parks schedule. Camping, cabins, yurts, boat launching and reservations charge separately.
launch-va-virginia-beach-first-landing-s.accessibility: The visitor center, amphitheater and paved approaches are accessible; a beach mat, beach wheelchair and reservable all-terrain wheelchair support wider access. Natural trails, sand and the Narrows remain uneven.
launch-va-virginia-beach-first-landing-s.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed, and proof of current rabies vaccination should be available. Keep pets away from wildlife, hot sand and crowded swimming areas.
launch-va-virginia-beach-first-landing-s.family: The calm-looking Chesapeake Bay beach, playgrounds, nature exhibits and short Bald Cypress loop can work well for families, but swimming is at your own risk with no lifeguards.
launch-va-virginia-beach-first-landing-s.transit: Seasonal WAVE service reaches the Shore Drive area. Confirm current routing and the correct side of Shore Drive; the two main activity zones are separated by a busy roadway.
launch-va-virginia-beach-first-landing-s.need: Arrive early on warm weekends. The Chesapeake Bay beach has no lifeguards, strong currents make swimming at the Narrows inadvisable, and cabins are closed during a major renovation project; verify the official reservation inventory rather than relying on an old reopening date. The adjacent military training center may create loud noise at any hour without posing danger to park guests.

launch-va-virginia-beach-mount-trashmore.summary: A nationally recognized former landfill transformed into a 165-acre city park with a 60-foot summit, two lakes, a huge inclusive playground, skate park, fitness routes and picnic facilities.
launch-va-virginia-beach-mount-trashmore.hours: The park follows posted Virginia Beach city-park hours, generally sunrise to sunset. Lighted facilities, programs and special events may use different schedules.
launch-va-virginia-beach-mount-trashmore.parking: Free parking is distributed along Edwin Drive and around the main recreation areas. The South Boulevard lot is permanently closed during the Windsor Woods stormwater project, so navigate to the Edwin Drive entrance.
launch-va-virginia-beach-mount-trashmore.arrival: Use 310 Edwin Drive for the mountain, Kids Cove, skate park and Lake Trashmore. Do not route to the closed South Boulevard lot when trying to reach Lake Windsor.
launch-va-virginia-beach-mount-trashmore.restrooms: Restrooms and seasonal concessions serve the central developed park. Confirm building availability for early-morning, late-day or event visits.
launch-va-virginia-beach-mount-trashmore.cost: Ordinary park, hill, playground, skate park, paths and shore fishing access are free. Shelter reservations, programs, concessions and special events may charge.
launch-va-virginia-beach-mount-trashmore.accessibility: Kids Cove uses a rubber surface and includes play components for varied abilities, including a wheelchair swing. Paved routes circle developed areas, while summit slopes are steep and exposed.
launch-va-virginia-beach-mount-trashmore.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed under city park rules. Keep them away from playground surfacing, crowded events, waterfowl and anglers.
launch-va-virginia-beach-mount-trashmore.family: Kids Cove has separate play zones, slides, elevated walks, climbers and swings. The summit is popular for kite flying and views, but children need supervision on slopes and beside both lakes.
launch-va-virginia-beach-mount-trashmore.transit: Hampton Roads Transit serves the Town Center area, followed by a walk to Edwin Drive. Check the current stop and pedestrian route before relying on transit.
launch-va-virginia-beach-mount-trashmore.need: No swimming or wading is allowed in either lake. Fishing is from shore only with a Virginia freshwater license; kayaks are allowed only on Lake Windsor. Sledding is prohibited, and large events can close roads or consume parking.

launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-beach-.summary: Virginia Beach's free resort beach and three-mile oceanfront promenade pair a separate bike path with playgrounds, public restrooms, performance parks, monuments and direct Atlantic access.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-beach-.hours: The beach and boardwalk are publicly accessible throughout the day, subject to emergency and event closures. Lifeguards generally staff the Oceanfront from 9:30 a.m. to at least 6:00 p.m. between Memorial Day weekend and Labor Day weekend.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-beach-.parking: Use a city garage, municipal surface lot or legal metered space in the Resort Area. Rates are dynamic in 2026, so compare the live city parking map rather than relying on an old flat rate; garages are usually simpler for a longer family visit.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-beach-.arrival: Choose a street number before leaving. Grommet Island and Rudee Inlet are at the south end, the fishing-pier area is near 15th Street, and King Neptune is at 31st Street; the general Oceanfront pin is not a useful meeting point.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-beach-.restrooms: Permanent public restrooms are located at 2nd, 17th, 20th, 24th, 30th and 31st streets. Seasonal operating conditions and maintenance can affect individual facilities.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-beach-.cost: Beach, boardwalk, bike path, monuments and city parks are free. Parking, rentals, fishing-pier access, food, concerts and ticketed events charge separately.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-beach-.accessibility: The boardwalk is paved and Grommet Island provides an accessible beach playground and access route. Beach wheelchairs and access mats are available at selected locations; sand conditions still vary.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-beach-.dogs: From Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day, leashed dogs may use the boardwalk from 6:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m., but dogs are not allowed on the Resort Area sandy beach from Rudee Loop to 42nd Street. North and south beaches allow dogs before 10:00 a.m. or after 6:00 p.m. Off-season, dogs may use the beach and boardwalk throughout the day; boardwalk leashes and cleanup rules still apply.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-beach-.family: Lifeguarded summer zones, Grommet Island, street-end playgrounds and frequent restrooms make the central Oceanfront practical for families. Keep children within arm's reach in surf and separate from the bicycle path.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-beach-.transit: Seasonal WAVE trolleys and Hampton Roads Transit serve the Resort Area. Walking and biking are effective once parked, but bicycles and surreys belong on the separate bike path, not the boardwalk.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-beach-.need: There is no single best Oceanfront entrance. Glass, public alcohol consumption and many disruptive activities are prohibited; storms, rip currents, special events and military aircraft noise can change the experience quickly. Check flags and lifeguard direction before swimming.

launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-aquari.address: 717 General Booth Boulevard, Virginia Beach, VA 23451
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-aquari.summary: A city marine-science campus with sharks, sea turtles, harbor seals, Chesapeake Bay habitats, a nature trail, boat excursions and a separately operated aerial adventure park.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-aquari.hours: The Aquarium is open daily 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m., except Thanksgiving, Christmas Day and inclement-weather closures. General-admission entry ends at 3:30 p.m.; member entry ends at 4:00 p.m.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-aquari.parking: Aquarium lots charge $6 per vehicle from April 1 through October 31 and are free November through March; members park free year-round. Use the North Building lot for the main entrance and boat dock.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-aquari.arrival: Reserve a timed ticket online and arrive within the selected entry window. The Aquarium campus, boat dock and Adventure Park use related but distinct check-in points and tickets.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-aquari.restrooms: Restrooms and family facilities are available inside the Aquarium. There is no re-entry after leaving, so complete restroom, food and stroller needs before exiting the ticketed area.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-aquari.cost: Current general admission is $35 for adults 18-69, $30 for seniors 70+, $30 for ages 5-17 and free for ages 0-4. Parking, boat trips, films, programs and the Adventure Park cost separately.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-aquari.accessibility: The Aquarium is ADA compliant, with accessible parking and manual wheelchairs available from Guest Services in exchange for photo identification. Strollers wider than 36 inches may not fit some doorways.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-aquari.dogs: Pets are not permitted inside the Aquarium; trained service animals follow the Aquarium's accessibility policy. Do not leave animals in vehicles.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-aquari.family: Most families should allow two to three hours, plus an additional hour for a program. Timed entry reduces crowding, but popular windows can sell out and there is no same-day re-entry.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-aquari.transit: Hampton Roads Transit and seasonal visitor routes serve the General Booth corridor. Confirm the current stop and allow time to cross the campus safely.
launch-va-virginia-beach-virginia-aquari.need: Buy ahead because timed windows can sell out. Check the renovation page for exhibit closures, arrive by 3:30 p.m., and remember that boat tours and the Adventure Park are separate experiences rather than included general-admission exhibits.

launch-va-virginia-beach-back-bay-nation.summary: A remote barrier-island ecosystem linking Back Bay National Wildlife Refuge's wetlands and wildlife-only beach recreation to roadless False Cape State Park and its primitive camps, historic settlement and six miles of oceanfront.
launch-va-virginia-beach-back-bay-nation.hours: Refuge grounds are open one-half hour before sunrise until one-half hour after sunset. False Cape is open sunrise-sunset and its visitor center is generally open 9:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m.; visitors traveling through the refuge must exit within 30 minutes of sunset.
launch-va-virginia-beach-back-bay-nation.parking: Day visitors use the small Back Bay Visitor Center lot. It fills quickly in summer. False Cape campers and overflow visitors use Little Island City Park; trailers cannot use the refuge lot and Little Island charges seasonally.
launch-va-virginia-beach-back-bay-nation.arrival: There is no public vehicle access to False Cape. Reach it on foot, bicycle, paddle craft or a reserved tram from Back Bay; the land route is about six miles and seasonal trail closures can force travel on soft ocean sand.
launch-va-virginia-beach-back-bay-nation.restrooms: Back Bay has visitor-center and selected trailhead facilities. False Cape has a visitor center, pit toilets and primitive campground water arrangements, but no restaurant, laundry, modern campground utilities or dependable facilities along the route.
launch-va-virginia-beach-back-bay-nation.cost: Back Bay charges $5 per vehicle from April 1 through October 31; hikers and bicyclists enter free and federal passes are accepted. False Cape itself has no day-use entrance fee, but parking, tram tours and camping may charge.
launch-va-virginia-beach-back-bay-nation.accessibility: Back Bay provides accessible visitor facilities and a D-Pool fishing platform. False Cape's visitor center is accessible and a beach wheelchair is available, but deep sand, long distances and primitive conditions sharply limit independent mobility.
launch-va-virginia-beach-back-bay-nation.dogs: Pets are never permitted in Back Bay National Wildlife Refuge except service dogs. Although False Cape allows leashed pets, they cannot pass through Back Bay; pet access must be by boat or from the North Carolina boundary.
launch-va-virginia-beach-back-bay-nation.family: Back Bay's shorter boardwalks and wildlife overlooks can suit prepared families. The full journey to False Cape is not recommended for young children, inexperienced campers or anyone needing quick emergency medical access.
launch-va-virginia-beach-back-bay-nation.transit: This remote Sandbridge destination is not practical by ordinary transit. Arrange a vehicle, bicycle, paddle craft or reserved Blue Goose tram and leave a time buffer for the return before sunset.
launch-va-virginia-beach-back-bay-nation.need: Swimming, surfing and sunbathing are prohibited on Back Bay Refuge beach. The East Dike Trail is currently the open seasonal dike route; both dike trails close November 1-March 31, leaving beach travel as the land route to False Cape. Bring abundant water, sun and insect protection, and never underestimate distance, heat, soft sand or changing tides.

launch-va-norfolk-norfolk-botanical-gard.summary: A 175-acre accredited living museum with more than 60 themed gardens, extensive waterside paths, seasonal flowers, a children's adventure garden, tram tours and year-round programs.
launch-va-norfolk-norfolk-botanical-gard.hours: The Garden is currently open daily 9:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. through September 30. Seasonal daytime hours and evening-event schedules change later in the year, so check the dated admission calendar before traveling.
launch-va-norfolk-norfolk-botanical-gard.parking: Free visitor parking is available at the main entrance near Baker Hall. High-demand bloom periods and evening light events can require reserved arrival times and fill the closest spaces.
launch-va-norfolk-norfolk-botanical-gard.arrival: Use the main Azalea Garden Road entrance and start at Baker Hall. Choose the children's garden, rose and Japanese gardens, or a tram overview before walking because the property is large.
launch-va-norfolk-norfolk-botanical-gard.restrooms: Restrooms and water are available at Baker Hall and selected developed garden areas. Interior paths can be far from the entrance, so use facilities before a long loop.
launch-va-norfolk-norfolk-botanical-gard.cost: Norfolk Botanical Garden is a paid nonprofit attraction, with prices and reservation requirements varying by daytime season and special event. Discounts and reciprocal-garden programs require current identification.
launch-va-norfolk-norfolk-botanical-gard.accessibility: Many primary paths and visitor facilities are accessible, and tram options reduce walking. Some permeable paths slope between the Rose Garden, NATO Bridge and Wildflower Meadow; confirm mobility-device and tour arrangements in advance.
launch-va-norfolk-norfolk-botanical-gard.dogs: Pet dogs are currently admitted on Sundays only and nonmembers pay the posted dog fee in addition to human admission. Dogs cannot enter World of Wonders or the Butterfly House. Trained service animals follow the accessibility policy, with a safety exception around splash fountains.
launch-va-norfolk-norfolk-botanical-gard.family: World of Wonders is the primary children's destination and is currently scheduled 9:30 a.m.-6:30 p.m. through October 15. Its splash fountains are scheduled through September 30, weather permitting, so bring water shoes and a change of clothes.
launch-va-norfolk-norfolk-botanical-gard.transit: The garden sits near Norfolk International Airport but is easiest to reach by car or rideshare. Ordinary transit may require a long or impractical walk; verify current routing.
launch-va-norfolk-norfolk-botanical-gard.need: Reserve ahead for major blooms, holidays and evening light events. Free tram tours, paid boat tours, the Butterfly House, World of Wonders and splash fountains each have seasonal schedules; outdoor collections change dramatically by season, and airport noise is part of the setting.

launch-va-norfolk-town-point-park.summary: An eight-acre free downtown riverfront lawn and promenade that links fountains, public art, Nauticus, Waterside, the Elizabeth River Trail and Norfolk's largest festivals.
launch-va-norfolk-town-point-park.hours: The public waterfront is generally available daily outside posted closures. Festivals, fountain operation, cruise-ship security and private permits can change access and hours independently.
launch-va-norfolk-town-point-park.parking: Use a downtown Norfolk city garage such as Town Point or Main Street and walk to the riverfront. Event days use special rates and nearby spaces fill early; cruise calls can also change curb and accessible parking.
launch-va-norfolk-town-point-park.arrival: Approach from Waterside Drive for the main event lawn, or from the Elizabeth River promenade when walking from Nauticus or Waterside District. Check the Festevents calendar before expecting a quiet park visit.
launch-va-norfolk-town-point-park.restrooms: Portable restrooms, including accessible units, are installed for major events. On ordinary days, use open nearby visitor destinations rather than assuming permanent park restrooms are available.
launch-va-norfolk-town-point-park.cost: Ordinary park, promenade, fountain and river-view access is free. Some concerts, food festivals, parking, cruises and adjacent attractions require tickets or purchases.
launch-va-norfolk-town-point-park.accessibility: Town Point Park and TowneBank Fountain Park are accessible, with paved waterfront approaches and accessible spaces in city garages. Festival layouts can reroute paths and seating.
launch-va-norfolk-town-point-park.dogs: Animals other than service animals are generally not permitted during Festevents programs unless specifically posted. Check event rules before bringing a dog to the waterfront.
launch-va-norfolk-town-point-park.family: The open lawn, ships, fountain and river activity make an easy family stop, but supervise children closely at the unfenced working-harbor edge and during dense festivals.
launch-va-norfolk-town-point-park.transit: The Tide light rail, Hampton Roads Transit buses, ferries, Elizabeth River Trail and downtown sidewalks all serve the waterfront. Check event detours and ferry schedules.
launch-va-norfolk-town-point-park.need: This park changes character with the calendar. Harborfest, Sail250, wine and food festivals, fireworks and cruise calls can bring screening, crowds, ticket rules, temporary restrooms and road closures; verify the same-day event listing.

launch-va-norfolk-nauticus-and-battleshi.summary: Norfolk's maritime discovery center combines hands-on harbor exhibits, the free Hampton Roads Naval Museum and self-guided access aboard the massive Iowa-class Battleship Wisconsin.
launch-va-norfolk-nauticus-and-battleshi.hours: Nauticus is open Tuesday-Sunday 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. and closed Monday. Holiday, maintenance, weather and special-event schedules can vary.
launch-va-norfolk-nauticus-and-battleshi.parking: Use the adjacent Town Point Garage or another downtown city garage. Five onsite accessible spaces are first-come and are unavailable on cruise-ship days.
launch-va-norfolk-nauticus-and-battleshi.arrival: Enter Nauticus at 1 Waterside Drive for ticketing before boarding Wisconsin. Victory Rover cruises depart nearby but require their own time and ticket; arrive early enough to park and walk from the garage.
launch-va-norfolk-nauticus-and-battleshi.restrooms: Restrooms and elevators are available inside Nauticus. Shipboard facilities and circulation are limited, so use the museum facilities before climbing into less accessible sections.
launch-va-norfolk-nauticus-and-battleshi.cost: General admission is currently $19.95 for ages 13+, $16 for ages 3-12 and free for ages 0-2 with a reserved ticket. Guided ship tours and Victory Rover cruises cost extra; the Hampton Roads Naval Museum is free.
launch-va-norfolk-nauticus-and-battleshi.accessibility: Nauticus and Wisconsin's main deck are wheelchair accessible. Most interior ship routes involve steep ladders, narrow passages and high thresholds; the Ship Experience Access Room provides a virtual alternative.
launch-va-norfolk-nauticus-and-battleshi.dogs: Pets are not permitted inside Nauticus or aboard the ship; trained service animals follow accessibility and safety procedures. Confirm accommodations before arrival because ship spaces are unusual.
launch-va-norfolk-nauticus-and-battleshi.family: Hands-on maritime exhibits and the battleship work well for school-age children. Toddlers need close supervision, and adults should assess whether steep ladders and confined spaces are appropriate.
launch-va-norfolk-nauticus-and-battleshi.transit: The Tide light rail, buses, ferry, downtown sidewalks and Elizabeth River Trail reach the waterfront. The MacArthur Square light-rail area is a practical downtown approach.
launch-va-norfolk-nauticus-and-battleshi.need: The general ticket includes Nauticus and standard Battleship Wisconsin access, but specialized tours add fees. Wear secure shoes, keep both hands available on ladders and use the accessible main deck or virtual access room if climbing is unsafe.
